$comment: What this repository contributes to a running stack, and what a check may
believe about it. `checked` is proved against this repository by
internal/manifest/manifest_test.go in this repository's own CI; `declared` is
a statement nobody can verify and carries its own `why`.
THE CLAIM WORTH READING HERE IS `refuses_unauthenticated_v1`, AND IT EXISTS
BECAUSE THE OPPOSITE WAS WRITTEN DOWN. vouchryx's own manifest test says, in
a comment, that wardryx `starts happily with an empty environment and
installs a built-in admin key`. Measured 2026-08-28 by starting it with
`env -i`: the first half was true then and is false now, and the second half
was already false then (ParseKeys("") already returned a non-empty map, one
entry: devkey -> default/admin) though nothing here had actually checked it.
2026-09-06 (W1 security hardening): a bare `wardryx serve` with no
WARDRYX_KEYS and no WARDRYX_ALLOW_DEVKEY now REFUSES TO START rather than
installing the devkey fallback silently on whatever address -addr bound
(all interfaces, by default). `starts_with_empty_environment` flips to false
for exactly that reason, and `refuses_with_no_keys_and_no_allow_devkey`
replaces it as the checked claim about a truly empty environment. The old
false comment in vouchryx is corrected the same way it was found: by
running the thing, not by editing the comment that was wrong about it.
A false sentence about authentication, living in a comment in another
repository, is exactly what a per-repo manifest is for: the only place that
can settle it is the repository that owns the behaviour, and the only way to
settle it is to run the thing.

zero_policies_allows_every_request.value: no -policy given; running with zero policies, every request will be allowed
zero_policies_allows_every_request.why: It says this at startup, and it is a policy-plane default rather than an authentication one: a caller still needs a bearer key to ask, and with no policy loaded the answer to what it asks is allow. Declared rather than checked because what a launcher SHOULD supply is a deployment decision, not a fact about this repository.

no_db_means_approvals_are_lost_on_restar.value: no -db given; using an in-memory approval store (state is lost on restart)
no_db_means_approvals_are_lost_on_restar.why: Also said at startup. Not checked here because proving it would mean restarting the process and asserting an absence, and the sentence the process prints is the honest form of the same claim.
